name: Kitemoka
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: extinct Chapacuran; only Créqui-Montfort & Rivet 1913 vocabulary, no grammar

sources.citation: Lexibank CLDF dataset 'birchallchapacuran' (from Birchall, Dunn & Greenhill 2016), doculect kitemoka = kite1237.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 79 Kitemoka forms, all sourced CrequiMontfortRivet1913; segmented forms carry no stress marks.

sources.citation: Angenot-de Lima, Geralda. 1997. Fonotática e fonologia do lexema Protochapakura. Dissertação de Mestrado, UNIR Guajará-Mirim.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: §3.7 pp.48-52 'Fonemas e sons do Kitemoka' (source: CM&R 1913) gives a reinterpreted phoneme/allophone inventory and phonotactics only, with no stress remark; p.13 states the six dead languages incl. Kitemoka 'nunca tiveram seus sistemas fonológicos descritos'. The family-wide rule §2.2 p.24 (lexeme stress predictable from syllable weight, heavy final syllable stressed) is built on the five living languages, not on Kitemoka data.

sources.note: Already scanned for nape1237 (held by the project); contains Napeca and Chapacura lists but no Quitemoca list and no accent statement — listed only to record that it was checked and superseded.

sources.citation: Birchall, Joshua, Michael Dunn & Simon J. Greenhill. 2016. A combined comparative and phylogenetic analysis of the Chapacuran language family. International Journal of American Linguistics 82(3): 255-284.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress. Sec. 2 item 2 'Kitemoka' (p.257): primary data = d'Orbigny wordlist in CM&R 1913; one speaker recorded by Jürgen Riester in Concepción in the 1960s, partly transcribed in Wienold 2012; no speakers remain. Fn. 7 and sec. 4 use Wienold's phonemic readings of the Riester tape (<l'> = [z]/[j], <x> = /h/).

sources.citation: de Créqui-Montfort, Georges & Paul Rivet. 1913. Linguistique bolivienne. La famille linguistique Čapakura. Journal de la Société des Américanistes n.s. 10(1): 119-171.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Kitemoka (K) appears in the ethnohistory (p.121), the 'parenté évidente.. à peine dialectes' remark (p.125), grammatical notes pp.133-136 (suffixes -yu/-ko, no gender or plural per d'Orbigny, pronouns, negation -sa) and the comparative vocabulary pp.141-166 (97 K lines). No section on pronunciation or accent; transcription is referred (p.125 n.7) to the 1912 Otuké paper, whose note p.318 n.2 says the accented vowels mark d'Orbigny's 'nasal et guttural' vowel quality, not tonic accent. The one 'accentué' (p.133) means 'less pronounced' word-shortening.

sources.note: Nothing on accent. p.289: the Quitémocas speak the same language as the Chapacuras; finals mostly vowels, else k, m, t, p, j; guttural Spanish j common, nasal u; Spanish ch frequent; body-part suffix -ché in Quitemoca (Urutaraché, Tatiataché, Cuché); 'la tribu des Quitémocas possède beaucoup de termes entièrement différens de ceux des Chapacuras'.

sources.note: Comparative-historical stress reconstruction for the family (weight-sensitive, final heavy syllable) that would be the basis for any inference about Kitemoka; built on living languages, so at best second-hand for Kitemoka. Content restated in Lima 1997 §2.2 p.24 and Angenot-de Lima & Angenot 2000 (both held by the project under iten1243).

sources.citation: Riester, Jürgen. 1960s. Audio interview with a Kitemoka speaker, Concepción (Bolivia); unpublished recording (cited in Birchall, Dunn & Greenhill 2016: 257).
